desc: Compute cost[i] for every length-x window via sliding Fenwick (counts + sums) and kth order statistic; cost formula verified against naive median baseline.

Implement the selection DP with prefix minima: dp[t][i] = cost[i] + min_{p <= i-x} dp[t-1][p], returning min cost for exactly k non-overlapping windows (exactly-k == at-least-k since costs are nonnegative).
Execute the solution and confirm Example 1 -> 8 and Example 2 -> 3, plus edge cases (x==len(nums), k*x==len(nums), k==1, all-equal -> 0).
Random brute-force cross-check on ~11500 small/duplicate/negative/wide-value/maximal-packing inputs against a naive DFS reference (zero mismatches).

Confirm performance at n=10^5, k=15 with worst-case distinct values (Fenwick slide O(n log U) dominates; DP ~14*1e5 steps) and verify INF handling when DP states are infeasible (tight packing n=k*x) — all cases PASS, peak memory in the tens of MB.
